newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean industrials inch higher, more active.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean industrials inch higher, more active.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrials closed a touch firmer on Tuesday with brokers saying indications were that more investors were creeping back into the bourse after deserting it for the local money market in recent weeks.
The brokers said rates as high as 23 percent on the money market had lured most investors who were however coming back to the equities where shares had weakened to affordable levels.
"Today we saw a few individual and institutional buyers coming back into the market because most of the shares are now quite cheap. They had become rather expensive to buy," one broker commented.
The key industrial index put on a marginal 0.07 points to close at 10,028.25 on Tuesday.
Counters to advance included wine markers Afdis, which added 90 cents to 550 while cement company Porthold added 50 cents to 1,650 and multi-industrials TZI were up 25 cents to 1,025.
Other gains were in Hunyani Warrants and tobacco group TSL, which both put on 20 cents to 100 and 620 respectively.

Minings were slightly more active than the previous day but traded largely unchanged. However a 10 cent gain to 550 in coal producer Wankie nudged the seven-share secondary index there 1.13 points up to 1,015.49.
